findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_pages, get_events, search, submit_event, get_submission_status · Private data: submit_event, get_submission_status · Public sink: get_events, submit_event · Destructive: get_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_pages, get_events, search, submit_event, get_submission_status · Private data: submit_event, get_submission_status · Public sink: get_events, submit_event · Destructive: get_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_cities" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
